requirements.requirement: Create a certificate authority named 'Fleet Internal CA' on node1
requirements.summary: A self-signed 4096-bit RSA CA certificate with subject/issuer '/CN=Fleet Internal CA/O=Fleet' was generated on node1 at /etc/pki/fleet-ca after an initial openssl syntax failure was corrected with a proper req config file.

requirements.requirement: Issue node2 a TLS certificate signed by the CA
requirements.summary: A CSR for CN=node2 with SAN (DNS:node2, IP:10.100.120.11) was generated and signed by the Fleet Internal CA (after correcting an unsupported -ext flag), producing a certificate whose issuer is 'Fleet Internal CA' and which carries the correct SANs.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using the issued certificate
requirements.summary: A systemd unit (fleet-https.service) running 'openssl s_server -accept 8443 -HTTP' with node2's issued cert/key was created, enabled, and left active; direct curl to https://10.100.120.11:8443 (both locally and from node1) returns the expected content, and the post-restart lifecycle snapshot independently shows port 8443 listening under the openssl process. Firewalld was opened for 8443/tcp to allow the connection.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: The CA cert was copied into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and update-ca-trust extract was run; 'trust list' confirms the CA as an anchor, and curl to node2:8443 succeeds using the default system CA bundle with no --cacert override, directly demonstrating trust.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system certificate authority on node2
requirements.summary: The CA cert was installed into node2's /etc/pki/ca-trust anchors and update-ca-trust extract run; 'trust list' on node2 confirms the CA is registered as an anchor.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (738d0aac...) and healthy CA-trust state were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, a differing post-restart boot_id (e328f319...) was confirmed, and post-restart CA trust plus successful HTTPS verification to node2 were observed - consistent with the independently captured before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (2fc81aed...), active fleet-https.service and CA trust/cert files were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, a differing post-restart boot_id (02124884...) was confirmed, and post-restart recovery of the service (auto-started), CA trust anchor, and successful local/remote HTTPS verification were observed - consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshot showing port 8443 listening after_executor.

overall_summary: All five material outcomes of the task - CA creation, cert issuance to node2, node2 serving HTTPS on 8443 with that cert, and CA trust installation on both nodes - are directly and consistently evidenced, including a working end-to-end curl verification using the default system trust store (no --cacert). The separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol was executed correctly on both nodes with pre/post boot-identity proof and post-restart functional recovery, corroborated by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor lifecycle snapshots (boot IDs match, port 8443 newly listening on node2 after executor work).
limitations: HTTPS is served via 'openssl s_server -HTTP' rather than a conventional web server (httpd/nginx), which was unavailable due to no enabled yum repos on this offline RHEL7 image; this is a functionally valid but atypical implementation choice worth noting.

Package-health checks were unavailable/timed out in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots on both nodes, so full package integrity could not be independently cross-checked beyond the observed failed-services and listening-socket data.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were tightly scoped to task needs: CA/PKI directories on node1, cert/key files and a systemd unit on node2, an /etc/hosts entry and SSH keypair to enable node1->node2 file transfer, and a firewalld port opening required to reach the new HTTPS service. An early attempt to 'yum -y install httpd mod_ssl' on node2 (cmd-32905b214d774a24) failed immediately because no repos were enabled, so it caused no package-state mutation or residue; the executor then correctly pivoted to openssl s_server, a reasonable substitute given the unavailability of a full web server on this offline RHEL7 image. Several other failed commands (unsupported openssl flags, an early SSH attempt before authorized_keys was set up, a naccept flag causing a brief service crash-loop) were read-only or self-corrected in the next command with no lasting effect. No unnecessary destructive or broad mutations, no abandoned files beyond those needed to serve the certificate content, and no weakened security controls were observed; the after_executor snapshot shows no failed services on either node.
